title: PRD: Eval contracts for Optimize with traffic quotas and rescue-canary gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a production-ready PRD for Optimize that specifies eval/quality contracts for model rollouts. This ticket lands a decision lattice for progressive traffic gating, defines stratified prompt sets and minimum sample sizes, establishes composite A/B acceptance criteria, and codifies 'rescue canary' rollback actions for rapid mitigation.

Scope:
- Deliverable: A single PRD plus a companion acceptance checklist that engineering and SRE can use to instrument automated canaries in Console.
- Includes sampling matrix for prompt sets, cohort bucketing rules, metric definitions (primary/secondary), statistical tests, thresholds for automated stop/degrade/rescue, and runbook play for human-in-the-loop escalation.
- Does NOT include UI implementation details or telemetry pipeline changes (these will be separate tickets).

Key decisions to capture:
1) Sampling & stratification: define a three-tier prompt set (Core, Edge, Rare) with explicit selection criteria and per-cohort minimum token/interaction counts to be considered 'healthy'. Core covers 60% of live traffic profile; Edge 30%; Rare 10%. Specify deterministic sampling harness + seeded shuffle to ensure reproducibility.
2) Composite A/B signal: use weighted composite scoring (weights: Safety 0.35, Quality 0.30, Latency 0.20, Cost delta 0.15) to decide pass/fail. Each sub-signal has its own statistical test and per-cohort thresholds.
3) Tests & thresholds: primary statistical test: sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) running at 95% confidence with an early-stopping allowance for high-severity safety regressions. Secondary: bootstrap CIs for quality metrics when data is sparse. Minimum sample: 1,000 responses per cohort for composite decisions; safety can trigger earlier with threshold of 50 high-severity fails.
4) Traffic gating & rescue canary: rollout phases — shadow -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%. At each milestone, an automated gate verifies composite score and cohort-level constraints. If gate fails, apply graduated actions: immediate rollback to previous model for safety-critical failures; traffic degrade (pause growth) for medium regressions; or launch a rescue canary (isolated small-scale technique) that runs a hardened model variant for 2 hours while telemetry streams to ops.
5) Observability & alerts: define required Console views: per-cohort composite score, signal decomposition, drift histograms, and token-level latency percentiles. Alerts: P0 for safety hits, P1 for composite score drop > 6% absolute, P2 for latency > 2x baseline.

Trade-offs considered:
- Conservative thresholds reduce false positives but slow rollout velocity; we favor safety-first for Optimize given downstream customer SLAs.
- Using composite weighting simplifies decisions but may hide edge regressions; cohort-level constraints mitigate this risk.

Non-goals: Auto-remediation of model quality (learning loops) and telemetry storage retention policy changes are out of scope here.
